answer: In an agent marketplace selling onyx carvings, raven illustrations, and crystal ornaments, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents gives the attacker exactly the same voting power as staking them in one account. Gaining more influence requires buying and locking more tokens, tying up capital and exposing it to price risk for the full lock period.
